transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess my family thinks I got a little carried away. I was working on the house, trying to make it look nice with wood and lights and display things. I did use some of our savings for it, which… I know doesn’t sound great.

But at the time it felt important, like if I stopped working—even after it got dark—the house, maybe the whole block, would miss its chance. I was just trying to do something good, you know?
Can you describe how you were feeling during that time you were working on the house? Were you more energetic or excited than usual?

Yes, I’d say I had more energy than usual. Most days I felt… charged up, almost happy, like I was young again and could really get things done. It didn’t feel bad to me at the time.

I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was out of control, Doctor, but if my wife or one of the contractors questioned what I was doing, I’d get heated pretty quick. I’d start yelling, and then later I’d feel a little embarrassed about it. But mostly I felt excited, like I was on a mission.
During the time you were working on the house and feeling more energetic and excited, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure, Doctor. I mean… I was up late working some nights, but I don’t know if I’d say I needed less sleep exactly. I just got caught up in what I was doing.

Maybe my wife would say I was sleeping less, but I wasn’t really keeping track. Is that what you mean?
During this time, did you find that you could function well with much less sleep than usual, even if you were up late working?

I don’t know that I could say that for sure, Doctor. I mean, I was up late, yes, but I wasn’t really thinking, “Oh, I don’t need sleep.” I just wanted to finish what I was doing.

Maybe I managed okay for a while, but I’m not sure how much sleep I was actually getting. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.
Looking back, do you think you actually needed less sleep during that time, like you felt rested even if you slept only a few hours?

I’m not real sure, Doctor. Looking back, I can’t honestly say I felt rested on just a few hours. I know I stayed up late sometimes because I was wrapped up in the work, but whether I actually needed less sleep… I don’t know.

I don’t want to overstate it or tell you something that isn’t right. Maybe I was pushing myself more than usual, but I can’t say for sure I felt fine on hardly any sleep.
Looking back, was there a time when you felt you could get by on very little sleep—like only a few hours a night—without feeling tired the next day?

I wish I could give you a clear yes or no, Doctor. I don’t really remember feeling like I only slept a couple hours and then felt just fine the next day.

I know I stayed up too late some nights, but I can’t honestly say I wasn’t tired or that I needed hardly any sleep. Maybe I wasn’t paying close enough attention. Does that make sense?
Looking back, did you ever feel like you didn’t need much sleep at all — like you could function just fine even if you only slept a couple of hours?

I’m sorry, Doctor, I still don’t feel sure enough to say that. I mean, I may have had nights where I didn’t sleep much, but I don’t really remember feeling like I could just run on a couple hours and be perfectly fine.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was or give you the wrong impression. I just can’t say for certain that I didn’t need sleep.
Can you recall if there was a time when your mood was so high or irritable that it was noticeably different from your usual self, lasting for several days in a row?

Yes… I think so, Doctor. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days I’ve felt kind of charged up, almost happy in a way I haven’t felt in years—like I’m young again.

But then, if my wife or the contractors question me about things, I get hot fast. I start yelling before I really mean to. I know that’s not like how I usually try to be. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you tell me if there was a period when you felt unusually upbeat or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week—like a constant mood rather than just occasional moments?

Yes, Doctor… I think that’s fair to say. It hasn’t just been little moments here and there. Most days I’ve felt kind of charged up—almost joyful, like I’m young again.

I don’t mean I’m trying to be difficult, but when my wife or the contractors question me, I get hot pretty fast and start yelling. I’m not proud of that. But yes, it does feel like it’s been there most of the day, nearly every day.
Can you tell me if you felt driven to keep working on the house, even when others thought you should stop or rest — like you couldn’t slow down even if you wanted to?

Yes… I suppose I have been like that. I don’t mean I’m doing anything wild, Doctor, just trying to keep busy and get things done.

But I can’t seem to just sit in the chair anymore. I’m up and down all day, going from the garden to the darkroom to the porch, carrying tools around, fixing little things before anyone even asks me to. If someone tells me to rest, I’ll say I will, but then I’m back on my feet again.

I don’t know if that’s what you mean by driven, but… yes, it’s been hard to slow myself down.

F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood) is ruled out as the symptoms exceed a stress response and meet criteria for a manic episode.
